title: Align failure-handling contracts across runtime & SDKs (retries, backoff, idempotency, hedging)
text:
Align failure-handling contracts across runtime & SDKs (retries, backoff, idempotency, hedging)

description:
Problem: Different Redwood components (serving runtime, public SDKs, internal agent libraries) implement divergent retry, timeout, and backoff semantics. This leads to surprising end-to-end behavior: duplicate side-effects when idempotency is unclear, ineffective hedged requests that bypass server-side circuit breakers, and unclear failure signals for the Console and SLO alerts. Goal: produce a single failure-handling contract and migration plan that standardizes defaults and extension points for retries, backoff, hedging, timeouts, and idempotency keys across runtime and SDKs so that behavior is predictable, observable, and compatible with multi-region failover and load-shedding policies.

acceptance_criteria:
A canonical spec doc exists describing: client-side semantics (retryable error classes, default timeouts), header-level idempotency token semantics, hedged request behavior, and interaction with server-side circuit breakers and load-shedding.
Runtime accepts and enforces the contract: honors idempotency header, de-duplicates based on token when configured, exposes explicit error codes for transient vs. permanent failures.
SDKs (JS + Python + Go) implement the agreed default policy and provide a clear opt-in for hedging and per-request overrides via a single config object.
All call paths instrument metrics that map to SLOs: retry_attempts, retried_errors, hedged_requests, idempotency_hits, circuit_breaker_trips, client_timeouts. Dashboards updated and alerted.
Backward-compatible rollout plan with a two-week opt-in period followed by gradual enforcement with feature flag enforcement on dedicated and hosted customers.
Runbook updated: how to diagnose duplicate processing, how to disable hedging per-customer, and steps to roll back enforcement.
No regressions in latency SLOs for top 10 production routes (validated on canary traffic).

approach:
Phase 0 - Discovery: inventory all existing retry and hedging code paths in runtime + SDKs; capture current defaults and header semantics (expected by 2026-03-05).
Phase 1 - Contract design: author a single 'Failure Handling Contract' that defines: idempotency token header name, canonical error classification (TRANSIENT, PERMANENT, THROTTLE, SERVER_BUSY), per-request timeout vs overall deadline, retry/backoff algorithm defaults, hedging semantics (parallel vs speculative), and circuit-breaker signals to honor.
Phase 2 - Runtime changes: add endpoint-level flags to honor idempotency tokens, return canonical error classes, and expose a compatibility mode header for older SDKs.
Phase 3 - SDK changes: implement client-side policy object with sensible defaults: exponential backoff with jitter (base=50ms, max=2s, max_attempts=3), hedging disabled by default but available as opt-in, and an idempotency helper that ties into request builders.
Phase 4 - Telemetry & dashboards: instrument metrics and tracing spans for retry lifecycle and hedged request branches. Create SLO-linked dashboards and heatmaps for multi-region failovers.
Phase 5 - Rollout: feature-flag the enforcement on runtime; coordinate SDK releases; run a staged opt-in with a canary that uses strict enforcement for internal traffic first.
Phase 6 - Post- rollout: run a two-week monitoring window and collect customer feedback; treat any burst of duplicate side-effects as a P0 for rollback investigation.

rollout_plan:
Week 1: Publish RFC and compatibility matrix; ship runtime feature-flag (opt-in). Notify customers with guidance and migration steps.
Week 2: Publish SDK minors that support the new config object; make hedging opt-in and idempotency helpers available.
Week 3: Enable enforcement for internal canaries (10% internal traffic) and validate metrics and duplicate-event rate.
Week 4: Expand canary to dedicated customers who opt-in via console toggle; collect telemetry and support feedback.
Week 5-6: If stable, flip enforcement default for hosted API (soft-commit) while keeping an escape hatch header for older clients for 30 days.
Rollback: clear steps in runbook to flip feature-flag off and rapidly revoke hedging from client-side SDKs via server-side header.

telemetry:
Metric names: redwood.retry.attempts, redwood.retry.success_after_retry, redwood.hedge.requests, redwood.idempotency.dedup_hits, redwood.circuit.breaker.trips, redwood.client.timeouts
Span annotations: retry_attempt_n, hedge_branch, idempotency_token=<hash>, server_error_class
Dashboards: per-route retry heatmap, hedging effectiveness (latency vs success delta), idempotency dedup rate, circuit-breaker triggers by region
Alerts: increase in idempotency dedup_hits by >0.1% over baseline OR spike in duplicate side-effects in downstream systems

blockers:
Need sign-off from Security for idempotency token format and storage guidance (PII risk).
Runtime team needs a short API to expose canonical error class; depends on kernel scheduling release schedule.
Console/Customer Success coordination: messaging and toggle UX before enabling enforcement for hosted customers.

comments:
2026-03-02 | Marcus Chen: Completed inventory of JS & Python SDK retry code paths. Found divergent default max_attempts (JS=4, Py=2) and mismatched backoff windows.
2026-03-04 | Aisha Patel: Security raised a question about persistent idempotency token storage in logs. Added requirement: always hash tokens before persisting and mark PII flag.
2026-03-07 | Liz Romero (SRE): Suggested exposing a soft-fail header so older SDKs receive a deprecation-warning response without enforcement for 30 days.
2026-03-10 | Marcus Chen: Drafted RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FAILURE-HANDLING-CONTRACT (internal). Please review by 2026-03-17.
2026-03-12 | Design review with Console team: agreed to add a per-customer 'disable hedging' toggle in the tenancy UI for dedicated customers.
